outputs.exact_statement: Every $n$-point subset of a real $L_p$ space embeds isometrically into $\ell_p^{\binom n2}$. This holds for every $1\le p<\infty$.

Let $G$ be a connected loopless graph on $n\ge2$ vertices, let $B$ be an oriented edge-by-vertex incidence matrix, and let $C=\operatorname{diag}(c_e)$ with $c_e>0$. If $Q$ is the Euclidean orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}(C^{1/2}B)$, then $$\label{eq:localization}
  \bigl\|\,|Q|\,\bigr\|_{2\to2}\le 2\log n.$$

For every strictly positive probability vector $\lambda$ on $E$, there is a probability vector $\sigma$ with $\sigma_e\ge\lambda_e/2$ such that the orthogonal projection $P$ onto $V$ in $\ell_2(\sigma)$ satisfies $$\label{eq:projection-row-sums}
 \max_{e\in E}\sum_{f\in E}|P_{ef}|\le H.$$ In particular, $\|P\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le H$, and both $P$ and $I-P$ are contractions on $\ell_2(\sigma)$.

Let $h$ be a bounded real function supported on a region of finite $\nu$-measure, and let $S$ be its signed Poisson sum. For $q>2$ and $\epsilon>0$, $$\label{eq:poisson-moments}
 \int|h|^q\,d\nu
 \le\mathbb E|S|^q
 \le(1+\epsilon)\int|h|^q\,d\nu
   +C_{q,\epsilon}\left(\int h^2\,d\nu\right)^{q/2}.$$

outputs.exact_statement: There exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone has no finite semidefinite lift.

The polynomial $p_Q$ is homogeneous of degree $n(n+1)$ and hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_n,I_n,0)$, with $p_Q(e)=1$. Fix $y$ and choose vectors $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in\mathbb R^r$ with $Q(y)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_jb_j^\top$. Define $$B_j=\begin{pmatrix}0&b_j^\top\\-b_j&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \mathcal B=\begin{pmatrix}B_1\\\vdots\\B_n\end{pmatrix}.$$ Then the closed hyperbolicity cone $K_Q$ of $p_Q$ is characterized, at this value of $y$, by $$\label{eq:block-cone}
 (X,Z,y)\in K_Q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \begin{pmatrix}I_n\otimes X&\mathcal B\\
                 \mathcal B^\top&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.$$

The set $E_Q$ is the image of the affine section $K_Q\cap\{X=\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(1,A):A\in\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}_r\}$ under the projection $(X,Z,y)\mapsto(A,Z_{00},y)$. Consequently, if $K_Q$ is a spectrahedral shadow, then so is $E_Q$.

There is a positive semidefinite matrix $T\in\mathcal H$ of rank $d_*=20$ with the following properties. Its restriction to $L$ is positive definite. If $$J=\ker T,\qquad K=\operatorname{proj}_P J,
 \qquad H_0=\{p\in H:T(p,L)=0\},$$ then $\dim K=k=16$, multiplication $$\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}^2K\longrightarrow\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_7]_4$$ is injective, and $$\label{eq:pure-cubic-spanning}
 K\langle x_1,\ldots,x_7\rangle
   =\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_7]_3.$$ Finally, $JH_0$ has codimension $9$ in $\mathbb R[x]_4$.

The set $\mathcal X$ is a smooth semialgebraic manifold of dimension $$D=330-1-\frac{k(k+1)}2=193.$$ Before projectivization, the tangent space at a representative $Y$ is the space of $Y'\in\mathcal H$ whose restriction to $\ker Y\times\ker Y$ is zero.

For every $[Y]\in\mathcal X$, the map $$\Delta_{K_Y}:\mathbb R^7\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(K_Y,\mathbb R[s]_1), \qquad t\longmapsto(p\mapsto\partial_t p)$$ is injective, and the coefficient maps $a,b$ in [eq:kernel-graph] are not both zero. The seven infinitesimal translations and the infinitesimal dilation give eight independent variations of the kernel graph. These assertions, including the independence of the variations, also hold over $\mathbf C$ under the same rank and multiplication hypotheses.

The normalized matrices, together with their data $(K_Y,b,a)$, form a semialgebraic set $\mathcal M$ of dimension $185$. Normalization is continuous, and each $[Y]\in\mathcal X$ is uniquely recovered from its normalized data and its seven translation parameters and positive dilation parameter. Moreover, $\mathcal M$ has a compact ambient semialgebraic space in which the projection to $\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}(k,P)$ is continuous.

The matrix $T$ in Lemma 4 may be chosen so that, for $K=\operatorname{proj}_P\ker T$,* 1. *the fiber $\mathcal M_K$ of $\mathcal M\to\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}(k,P)$ is finite;* 2. *no point of $\overline{\mathcal M}\setminus\mathcal M$ projects to $K$.

Use the fixed decomposition $H=W\oplus K$ from [eq:fixed-complements]. Suppose $Y_i\in\mathcal H$ have blocks $$Y_i=\begin{pmatrix}A_i&B_i\\B_i^T&D_i\end{pmatrix},$$ where $A_i$ is invertible, $\sup_i\|A_i^{-1}\|<\infty$, and $$A_i^{-1}B_i\longrightarrow0, \qquad D_i-B_i^TA_i^{-1}B_i\longrightarrow0.$$ There are Hankel perturbations $\Delta_i\to0$ such that $Y_i^\sharp=Y_i+\Delta_i$ has rank $d_*$. Its $W$ compression $A_i^\sharp$ satisfies $$(A_i^\sharp)^{-1}-A_i^{-1}\longrightarrow0,$$ and $\ker Y_i^\sharp\to K$, or equivalently $\mathop{\mathrm{ran}}Y_i^\sharp\to W$.

Let $T,K,R,W$, and $\mathcal C$ be chosen as above. Suppose a sequence $Y_i\in\mathcal H$ has a group of $d_*$ eigenvalues bounded away from zero in absolute value, and the span of the corresponding eigenvectors tends to $W$. Suppose all remaining eigenvalues tend to zero. If the inverses of the compressions $A_i=(Y_i)_{W,W}$ converge to a nonzero matrix $C$, then $$[C]\in\mathcal C.$$
For $w$ and $U$ as in Lemma 11, let $$\mathcal S_U= \{(I_N\otimes Y)u: u\in U,\ Y\text{ a Hankel matrix on }H\}.$$ Then $w\notin\overline{\mathcal S_U}$.

There is an open ball $\Omega_0\subset\mathbb R^7$ about zero such that $M(s)$ has rank $N$ for every $s\in\Omega_0$. The polynomial map $$\label{eq:polynomial-patch}
 x(s)=\bigl(M(s)M(s)^T,\ \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}(gG(y_s)),\ y_s\bigr)$$ has degree at most four and takes $\Omega_0$ into $E_Q$. Its values satisfy the trace inequality defining $E_Q$ with equality.

Let $n\ge1$ and $j\ge0$ be integers, let $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$, and let the linear functional $\lambda:\mathbb R[z]_{\le2j}\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\lambda(p^2)>0$ for every nonzero $p\in\mathbb R[z]_{\le j}$. For every integer $b\ge j$, there is an extension $\widetilde\lambda:\mathbb R[z]_{\le2b}\to\mathbb R$ such that $\widetilde\lambda(p^2)>0$ for every nonzero $p\in\mathbb R[z]_{\le b}$.

There is a nonempty open subset $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ and real analytic maps $u:\Omega'	o\mathbb R^
u$ and $F:\Omega'	o\mathbb R^{\ell	imes\ell}$ such that $$\label{eq:analytic-Gram-identity}
 \mathcal L(p(s),u(s))=F(s)F(s)^T\qquad(s\in\Omega').$$

Let $C$, $p$, and $\Omega$ be as in Lemma 16. Fix an integer $b\ge\max\{1,\deg p\}$ and a linear functional $\lambda:\mathbb R[z_1,\ldots,z_n]_{\le2b}\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $\lambda(1)=1$ and $\lambda(q^2)\ge0$ for all $q\in\mathbb R[z]_{\le b}$. There is a nonempty open subset $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ such that, for each $c\in\Omega'$, the points $$x_\varepsilon=\lambda_z\bigl(p(c+\varepsilon z)\bigr)$$ admit points $\widetilde x_\varepsilon\in C$, for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, with $$\label{eq:near-feasibility} \|\widetilde x_\varepsilon-x_\varepsilon\|=O(\varepsilon^b).$$ The implied constant may depend on $c$ and on the displayed data.

For the admissible quadratic matrix map $Q$ of [eq:constructed-Q], the set $E_Q$ is not a spectrahedral shadow. Consequently its associated entire closed hyperbolicity cone $K_Q$ is not a spectrahedral shadow.
